# Pandamonium v1.0.45

A new operator access-level control lets you choose how much the agent asks before acting — Ask for approval, Approve for me, or Full access — from a shield button next to the Jarvis sphere. The approval-card workflow itself is unchanged.

## MAD-885 — Authority: add operator access-level control (Ask / Approve for me / Full access)

### Problem

Every gated agent action required a manual approve/deny decision. The workflow is the safety net and stays, but there was no way to tell the agent that routine internet and file work should proceed without prompting.

### Implementation

A shield button to the left of the Jarvis sphere opens a compact three-option menu. **Ask for approval** keeps the current behavior: every gated effect prompts. **Approve for me** auto-allows read, reversible writes, external publication (internet use), and edits outside the workspace, while destructive actions, credential or authentication changes, privilege expansion, and purchases still prompt. **Full access** auto-allows every classified effect. The mode is stored per user server-side through the validated preferences endpoint, and the single authority gate resolves it for chat, voice, gateway, extension, and task surfaces alike. Hard policy denies are never bypassed: unauthenticated requests, disabled tools and privileges, plan mode, and unclassified capabilities stay blocked under every mode. The approval cards, receipts, revoke, and natural-language approve/deny are untouched.

### Product value and UI visibility

The shield button shows the current mode at a glance (amber for full access, green for approve-for-me) and the menu carries the exact option labels and descriptions. Selecting a mode updates immediately, persists across reloads, and reverts with an error if the server rejects it. The menu opens above the composer, dismisses on outside click or Escape, and stays usable at narrow widths. Work-budget and all other composer controls are unchanged.

### Verification

New deterministic coverage includes the per-mode decision matrix (including hard denies and denial receipts), preference validation and persistence, UI markup and module wiring, and a browser spec that clicks the shield, verifies the button sits left of the Jarvis sphere, checks all three labels, captures the persistence request, and confirms Escape dismissal. The full Python suite passes (5,611 passed, 5 skipped) and the full browser suite passes (97/97).

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

The mode defaults to Ask for approval, so existing behavior is unchanged until you choose otherwise. It is per-user and stored with the existing preferences. The staged email review setting (`agent_email_confirm`) is unaffected. Unknown or unreadable mode values fall back to the safe default. Installation remains operator-owned.
